item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
A number machine takes a number and operates on it.
When the Input Number is 5, the Output Number is 9, as shown below.

[Image: Number machine diagram]

When the Input Number is 7, which of these is the Output Number?
item.figure_description:
A diagram of a number machine showing four geometric shapes connected horizontally by arrows:
1. A square containing the number "5", with the text "Input Number" centered directly above it.
2. An arrow pointing right labeled "× 2" leads to a circle containing the number "10".
3. An arrow pointing right labeled "+ 2" leads to another circle containing the number "12".
4. An arrow pointing right labeled "− 3" leads to an equilateral triangle containing the number "9", with the text "Output Number" centered directly above it.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a piece of string curved both ends and a rule in cm with value from 1 to 10.]

If the string in the diagram above is pulled straight, which of these is closest to its length?
reference_items.figure_description:
A metric ruler and a folded piece of string above it. The ruler has major tick marks labeled from 1 to 10 with "cm" before the 1, and intermediate half-centimeter tick marks between each number.

The string is laid horizontally above the ruler with both ends folded back:
- The bottom-left end starts at the 4 cm mark and extends left to the 3 cm mark, where it loops around 180 degrees.
- The middle section runs continuously to the right from the 3 cm mark to approximately the 8 cm mark.
- At approximately the 8 cm mark, it loops around 180 degrees upward and extends back to the left, ending at approximately the 6.5 cm mark.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
2, 5, 11, 23, ...

Starting the pattern at 2, which of these rules would give each of the terms in the number pattern above?

options.label: A
options.text: Add 1 to the previous term and then multiply by 2.

options.label: B
options.text: Multiply the previous term by 3 and then subtract 1.

options.label: C
options.text: Multiply the previous term by 2 and then add 1.

options.label: D
options.text: Subtract 1 from the previous term and then multiply by 3.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
